help.title: User guide
help.subtitle: Click any card for step-by-step instructions and tips
help.subtitle~mac: Tailored for macOS shortcuts and settings · Click any card to learn more
help.subtitle~win: Tailored for Windows shortcuts and settings · Click any card to learn more
help.capture.title: Three capture modes
help.capture.summary: Snap regions, windows, or full screens quickly
help.capture.s1: Press your shortcut for Region, Window, or Full screen capture
help.capture.s2: Move the pointer to auto-highlight buttons, tables, and windows
help.capture.s3: Scroll the wheel to step up from a small element to the whole window
help.capture.s4: Click to lock the selection, or drag freely to draw your own box
help.capture.t1: Hold the modifier key while dragging to pause snap to edges for fine control
help.capture.t1~mac: Hold Option (⌥) while dragging to pause snap to edges for fine control
help.capture.t1~win: Hold Alt while dragging to pause snap to edges for fine control
help.capture.t2: In Window capture, press the same shortcut again to grab the current window
help.capture.t3: Saved files go to the folder chosen in Capture & recording settings
help.capture.t3~mac: After saving, click the notification button to reveal the file in Finder
help.capture.t3~win: After saving, click the notification button to open the folder in Explorer
help.markup.title: Markup, pin, and copy
help.markup.summary: Add shapes or mosaic, pin on screen, or copy immediately
help.markup.s1: Once locked, pick rectangle, arrow, text, or mosaic on the toolbar
help.markup.s2: Adjust color swatches and the stroke slider right above the bar
help.markup.s3: Click Copy or press Enter to copy and paste straight into documents
help.markup.s4: Click Pin to keep a floating reference image above other windows
help.markup.t1: After copying, paste directly into documents or slides
help.markup.t1~mac: After copying, press ⌘V to paste into Keynote, Docs, or chat
help.markup.t1~win: After copying, press Ctrl+V to paste into PowerPoint, Word, or chat
help.markup.t2: Drag a pinned image to move it, and scroll the wheel to resize
help.markup.t3: Click Draw on the result toast to zoom right into that area for drawing
help.draw.title: Draw on screen
help.draw.summary: Freeze the current screen and annotate with pens and shapes
help.draw.s1: Press the Draw shortcut to freeze your screen as a canvas
help.draw.s2: Pick Pen (P), Highlighter (M), Text (T), or Eraser (D)
help.draw.s3: Pause for 0.5 s at the end of a stroke to turn rough strokes into neat shapes
help.draw.s4: Press Esc to exit; your drawings stay ready to restore next time
help.draw.t1: Undo quickly and use [ or ] to step stroke thickness
help.draw.t1~mac: Press ⌘Z to undo, and use [ or ] to adjust stroke width
help.draw.t1~win: Press Ctrl+Z to undo, and use [ or ] to adjust stroke width
help.draw.t2: Use Reopen last anytime to bring back your previous drawing
help.draw.t3: Color keys (R, Y, G, O, B, L) work directly without opening the palette
help.board.title: Whiteboard
help.board.summary: Open a clean white or black board to explain ideas
help.board.s1: Press the Whiteboard shortcut to open a clean full-screen board
help.board.s2: Press W for a white board or K for a dark chalkboard
help.board.s3: Use pens, highlighters, shapes, and text as on the live screen
help.board.s4: Save or copy your board anytime to share class notes
help.board.t1: All Draw shortcuts for tools, undo, and colors work the same way
help.board.t2: On the black board, dark ink automatically turns light so it stays readable
help.zoom.title: Zoom
help.zoom.summary: Magnify live motion smoothly around your pointer
help.zoom.s1: Press the Zoom shortcut to magnify your live screen
help.zoom.s2: Scroll the wheel or trackpad between 1× and 8× zoom level
help.zoom.s3: Keep clicking and typing in underlying apps while zoomed in
help.zoom.s4: Press the Draw shortcut anytime to freeze and sketch at the current zoom
help.zoom.t1: Hold Shift while scrolling to pass scroll events through to the app below
help.zoom.t2: Watch the corner minimap to see where you are on the monitor
help.zoom.t3: Press Esc to return cleanly to 1× view
help.record.title: Screen recording
help.record.summary: Record a selected region or window smoothly as video
help.record.s1: Press the Record shortcut and pick a region, window, or monitor
help.record.s2: Only the area inside the red frame is recorded; elapsed time shows at the top
help.record.s3: Choose your microphone ahead of time under Settings › Capture & recording
help.record.s4: Press the same key or click Stop on the top pill to finish
help.record.t1: A red status dot shows whenever recording is in progress
help.record.t1~mac: A red dot on the menu bar icon means recording is active
help.record.t1~win: A red dot on the taskbar icon means recording is active
help.record.t2: Finished recordings open directly from your save folder
help.record.t2~mac: Click the notification button when done to reveal the video in Finder
help.record.t2~win: Click the notification button when done to open the video in Explorer
help.shortcuts.title: Shortcuts
help.shortcuts.summary: Customize keys anytime and press ? for an instant cheat sheet
help.shortcuts.s1: Press ? inside Capture, Draw, or Zoom to view shortcuts for that mode
help.shortcuts.s2: Click any row in Settings › Shortcuts and press your new key combo
help.shortcuts.s3: Press Esc to cancel recording or Backspace to clear a shortcut
help.shortcuts.s4: Press Undo inside Settings to revert a shortcut change right away
help.shortcuts.s4~mac: Press ⌘Z inside Settings to revert your last shortcut change
help.shortcuts.s4~win: Press Ctrl+Z inside Settings to revert your last shortcut change
help.shortcuts.t1: Function keys (F1–F3) may require the fn key depending on keyboard settings
help.shortcuts.t1~mac: On MacBooks you may need fn+F1 unless standard function keys are enabled in System Settings
help.shortcuts.t1~win: On laptops with Fn Lock, press Fn along with F1–F3 if media keys trigger instead
help.shortcuts.t2: Conflicts show an orange dot and three ready-to-use alternative suggestions
help.troubleshoot.title: Troubleshooting
help.troubleshoot.summary: Quick fixes for permissions, shortcut conflicts, zoom, and resets
help.troubleshoot.s1: Open the checkup section at the top of Settings › General first
help.troubleshoot.s2: Follow the button next to any orange dot or warning
help.troubleshoot.s3: Use Reset all in Settings › General › Data if you want a clean slate
help.troubleshoot.t1: If another app claims the same shortcut, the first app opened usually wins
help.troubleshoot.t2: Diagnostic logs never store window titles or personal file names
help.troubleshoot.item1Title~mac: Captures look blank or windows aren’t detected
help.troubleshoot.item1Title~win: F1 or F2 shortcuts don’t respond
help.troubleshoot.item1Desc: Check your permissions and shortcut status
help.troubleshoot.item1Desc~mac: Verify Screen Recording and Accessibility in System Settings. Screen Recording may require a relaunch after enabling.
help.troubleshoot.item1Desc~win: Another app like Snipaste or PowerToys may own the key. See How to turn off in Settings › General.
help.troubleshoot.item2Desc: Shortcuts may be paused or blocked by a conflict
help.troubleshoot.item2Desc~mac: Check the menu bar icon for an orange dot or dimmed state and verify Toggle shortcuts is on.
help.troubleshoot.item2Desc~win: Check the taskbar menu to confirm shortcuts are enabled and resolve any orange conflicts.
help.troubleshoot.item3Desc: Verify permission or scroll zoom level
help.troubleshoot.item3Desc~mac: Screen Recording permission is required for Zoom. Relaunch ShookShok after enabling it.
help.troubleshoot.item3Desc~win: Scroll the wheel up to zoom in; protected DRM windows may appear hidden for privacy.
help.troubleshoot.item4Title: Want to reset everything to defaults
help.troubleshoot.item4Desc: Open Settings › General › Data and click [Reset all]
